headline: Micron's union at its Taoyuan plant in Taiwan has voted to authorise a strike, but no date has been set.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: the union's vote was announced at a press conference, with the company and ministry responses.
importance_line: What changed: workers at Micron's Taiwan plant now have a legal mandate to strike, which matters most to those workers and to Micron; whether it turns into action depends on the board's proposals after its 8 to 9 Oct meeting, and the company says it will keep talking.
summary: Focus Taiwan (CNA) reports that the union at US memory chipmaker Micron's Taoyuan plant in Taiwan won strike authorisation, with 1,994 votes in favour, or 88.3 percent of all eligible members. No strike date is set, but Jerry Lin, chairman of the Taoyuan union, said a 'surprise strike' is among the options, and the dispute is over profit-sharing: the union wants 15 percent of Micron's operating profit shared with employees, and it rejected Micron's offer of at least NT$1.7 million in cash.
notes: Chunk source Reuters blocked (401); read on Focus Taiwan (CNA) full text, which does not credit Reuters. Micron, the chipmaker, is described for readers as a US memory chipmaker.
